answer.evidence: The crystal in rows 1-11 is decor sitting on the pedestal. Below it the stone cap widens from 12 px (row 12) to 14 px (rows 13-15), then narrows to 12 px (rows 16-17), 10 px (rows 18-19) and the 8 px shaft (rows 20-25). That is an ellipse-like plate overhanging the shaft, with a lighter front-edge line at row 16 and a dark brown band below it at rows 17-19 acting as eave shadow. The shaft front face runs from row 17 to row 30 (14 rows), with a widened base plinth at rows 26-30. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small crystal on a grey stone pedestal with only 14 distinct colours in total. That gives about 3-4 steps per material (crystal facets, pedestal stone), against about 5-6 per material in the well, stall and hedge references. The measured dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral dark line with no tint of the neighbouring material. The pedestal's tone does not account for this: the well and hedge references have tinted edges (33% and 0% neutral) and the candidate does not. The sticker-like outline plus the shallow ramps weigh against it. There are no flat fills (0% near-flat coverage), and 9 visible tones per tile matches the hedge. That is still well below the well (20) and stall (17), and the stone shows no per-block shading or grain. A careful artist would find it thinner and more outlined than the references, so it fails.

answer.evidence: The crystals on top (rows 1-11) are decor. A light front-edge line sits at row 16, followed by a brown band at rows 17-19 acting as the shadow below it. The shaft and flared base (rows 17-30) give a front face of about 14 rows.

The references that carry real material (hedge 0%, stall 1%, well 33%) have tinted or mixed edges. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small crystal on a grey stone pedestal. Each material ramp looks like about 3 steps: the crystal has a white highlight, a light blue and a mid blue, and the pedestal has a light grey, a mid grey and a dark grey. The Beodeul well, stall and hedge carry 5-6 steps per material with per-stone and per-tile detail. The measured dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline reads as a uniform dark grey/black line. It does not lean blue next to the crystal or warm next to the stone, which gives the sticker look. By contrast the hedge (0%), stall (1%) and well (33%) have tinted outlines. Visible tones per tile are 9, which matches the hedge but is well below the well (20) and stall (17). There are no large flat fills (0% flat coverage), but the pedestal faces have little grain or stone-by-stone shading. Overall it is clean but shallower and more sticker-like than the references, so it fails.
